name: Main South
headline: Three-deckers and Victorian houses
around Clark University and University Park.
answer: Main South is a neighborhood in southern Worcester named for Main Street, the city's central roadway, with Clark University and the 14.3-acre University Park near its center. Much of its street plan and housing dates from before 1900: three-deckers, multi-unit houses and Victorian single-family houses, several of them on the National Register. WRTA Routes 19 and 27 run along Main Street, and Union Station's commuter rail is downtown.
meta: Main South, Worcester: three-deckers and Victorian houses around Clark University and University Park, with WRTA buses along Main Street to downtown.

boundaries.text: Main South follows Main Street through southern Worcester, with commercial areas on Main Street and Park Avenue and residential streets such as Woodland, Freeland, Beaver, Beacon and Oread Streets around Clark University. The city does not publish a fixed boundary.

overview: In the late 1840s Eli Thayer bought pasture along southern Main Street and, in 1849, opened the Oread Collegiate Institute, one of the country's first colleges for women, on a 10-acre hill off Main Street. Building spread slowly, reaching the area of the future campus in the 1880s and 1890s, when Jonas Gilman Clark bought land for the university. The legislature chartered Clark University on March 31, 1887, and it opened in 1889. The city bought the land for University Park across Main Street in 1887 and 1889. By 1890 the area had major industry and hundreds of new multi-unit houses.

Most of Main South's physical structure was in place before the end of the 19th century, and its streets still show it. Victorian houses, many renovated, stand beside three-deckers. The Woodland Street Historic District, next to the Clark campus, holds 19 Victorian houses built from 1868 to about 1904 in Second Empire, Italianate, Gothic Revival, Queen Anne and Colonial Revival styles. Three Queen Anne triple-deckers of about 1892 face University Park on Crystal Street, and five Colonial Revival triple-deckers of about 1916 line Beaver Street; both groups were listed on the National Register in 1990. Main Street itself carries churches listed in 1980, including Pilgrim Congregational at 909 Main Street and St. Peter's at 935.

Clark University and the Main South Community Development Corporation work together through the University Park Partnership. The CDC has renovated multi-family houses as affordable rentals in the Beacon and Oread Street block east of campus, and in 2013 the Kilby-Gardner-Hammond project added a Boys and Girls Club with a gymnasium, a learning center, an Olympic-size pool and an athletic field, along with renovated affordable housing. University Park Campus School, a Worcester public school for grades 7 to 12 founded with Clark in 1997, is on Freeland Street, and Clark's Center for Media Arts, Computing and Design opened at 7 Hawthorne Street in 2023.

housing.text: Main South's housing is mostly 19th- and early 20th-century: three-deckers, multi-unit houses and Victorian single-family houses, many renovated. National Register groups include the 19 houses of the Woodland Street Historic District and the triple-deckers on Crystal Street (about 1892) and Beaver Street (about 1916). The Main South CDC develops and manages affordable rental and ownership housing, including renovated multi-family houses on Beacon and Oread Streets and in the Kilby, Gardner and Hammond Street area.

areas.name: Clark University and University Park
areas.line: Clark's National Register-listed campus, bounded by Maywood, Woodland and Main Streets, faces the 14.3-acre University Park across Main Street.

areas.name: Woodland Street Historic District
areas.line: Nineteen houses on Woodland Street between Charlotte and Oberlin Streets, with frontage on Hawthorne, Loudon and Norwood Streets, built from 1868 in Second Empire, Italianate, Gothic Revival, Queen Anne and Colonial Revival styles; listed in 1980.

areas.name: Beacon and Oread Streets
areas.line: A block east of campus where the Main South CDC renovated multi-family houses as affordable rentals; the C.H. Fitch and Edward Stark houses at 15 and 21 Oread Street are on the National Register.

areas.name: Kilby, Gardner and Hammond Streets
areas.line: Blocks rebuilt in a project completed in 2013, with a Boys and Girls Club, an athletic field, a gymnasium, an Olympic-size pool and renovated affordable housing.

commute.text: WRTA Route 19 (Webster Square to Clark University) and Route 27 (Auburn Mall) run along Main Street, and Route 825 is the Park Avenue Connector. The nearest commuter rail is Worcester station at Union Station downtown, the western end of the MBTA Framingham/Worcester Line to Boston's South Station.

places.name: University (Crystal) Park
places.line: A 14.3-acre city park at 965 Main Street, bought in 1887 and 1889, with Crystal Pond, walking trails, basketball, tennis and volleyball courts, a playground and a spray park opened in August 2025.

places.name: Clark University
places.line: A 72-acre campus chartered in 1887, with Jonas Clark Hall (1887), Goddard Library, the 658-seat Atwood Hall and the Kneller Athletic Center; the campus's historic core is on the National Register.

places.name: Oread Castle Park
places.line: A 3.2-acre city park at 20 Alden Street on the site of Eli Thayer's Oread Collegiate Institute (1849 to 1881), with basketball courts, fitness stations, a playground and a nature trail.

places.name: Crystal Street Historic District
places.line: Three Queen Anne triple-deckers of about 1892 at 30-34 Crystal Street, facing University Park, each with a gable-roofed entry porch on one side and a rounded bay with a conical roof at the other end; listed in 1990.

places.name: Beaver Street Historic District
places.line: Five Colonial Revival triple-deckers of about 1916 at 31-39 Beaver Street, near Clark, with three-story front porches; listed in 1990 under the Worcester Three-Deckers submission.

places.name: Main Street churches
places.line: South Unitarian (888 Main Street), Pilgrim Congregational (909 Main Street) and St. Peter's Catholic Church (935 Main Street), all listed on the National Register in 1980.

history.text: Eli Thayer opened the Oread Collegiate Institute, one of the first women's colleges in the country, on a hill off Main Street.
Clark University was chartered on March 31; the city began buying land for University Park the same year.
University Park Campus School, a public school for grades 7 to 12, opened on Freeland Street.
The Kilby-Gardner-Hammond project was completed, with a Boys and Girls Club, an athletic field and renovated affordable housing.

faq.q: Is there a median home price for Main South?
faq.a: The Warren Group reports Worcester only as a whole city, so there is no Main South figure. Citywide, the median single-family sale price for calendar year 2025 was $430,000, across 884 sales, according to its MA December 2025 Sales, Prices by Town report.

faq.q: What kind of housing is in Main South?
faq.a: Mostly 19th- and early 20th-century housing: three-deckers, multi-unit houses and Victorian single-family houses. Several groups are on the National Register, including the Woodland Street Historic District and the triple-deckers on Crystal and Beaver Streets.

faq.q: How do you get from Main South to the commuter rail?
faq.a: WRTA buses run along Main Street, including Route 19 and Route 27, toward downtown. The commuter rail stop is Worcester station at Union Station, the western end of the MBTA Framingham/Worcester Line.

faq.q: Which school district serves Main South?
faq.a: Worcester Public Schools. School assignment is set by the district by address; review the district's profile with DESE.

notes: Written 2026-10-22. Boundaries: neither the city nor Clark publishes a fixed line; the record uses the street names on Clark's University Park Partnership neighborhood page and Wikipedia's description (southern Worcester, named for Main Street). Wikipedia's Clark article says the campus is 'about 2 miles west of downtown'; that distance and direction were not used. The Oread Collegiate Institute opening year (1849) and Thayer's land purchase are from the city's Oread Castle Park page and Clark's page; Wikipedia's Main South article dates the purchase to the 1840s. Clark's page is the source for 'by 1890 ... hundreds of new multi-unit housing structures' and 'Victorian structures, many renovated, alongside three-deckers'. Clark campus NR boundary and the Main Street churches' listing dates are from Wikipedia's list of NRHP listings in southwestern Worcester; the churches' building dates and architects were not found and are omitted. The Woodland Street district's 'about 1904' end date reflects the Colonial Revival houses of about 1900 to 1904. Route 825 (Park Avenue Connector) is listed on the WRTA routes page as read on 2026-10-22, but the page gives no map, so its exact path through the neighborhood is not stated; highways left empty because no source places a highway in the neighborhood. Left out: the Worcester Market Building (Wikipedia gives 627 Main Street, the NRHP list 831 Main Street) because its address could not be reconciled; Granger Fields and Harrington House (Clark properties, details limited); Main South CDC unit counts ('hundreds', no exact figure on its site). No population is given because no source reports one for this boundary. Market set to null: the Warren Group lists Worcester only citywide. Schools: assignment is by address and set by the district; University Park Campus School is named as a public school only, not rated. Fair housing: the Wikipedia Main South article characterizes crime in the neighborhood and cites a police-sting news story; none of that was used. Clark's page uses 'revitalization' and describes who lives in the neighborhood ('a diverse mix of people'); the record describes the projects as buildings, fields and housing types instead. The Beaver Street article's notes on early occupants were left out. The Boys and Girls Club is described by its facilities, not by who uses it, and Clark's homebuying assistance for its employees was left out as a program for a defined group. Fact-check 2026-10-22: Verified Clark's University Park Partnership page (Thayer's pasture purchase; building reaching the campus area in the 1880s and 1890s; Jonas Clark's land; 'by 1890' major industry and hundreds of multi-unit housing structures; physical structure set before 1900; Victorian structures, many renovated, with three-deckers; the CDC's Beacon and Oread Street renovations; Kilby-Gardner-Hammond completed 2013 with its Boys and Girls Club, gymnasium, learning center, Olympic-size pool, athletic field and affordable housing; University Park Campus School, grades 7 to 12, 1997, Freeland Street), Clark University on Wikipedia (charter signed March 31, 1887; opened 1889; 72 acres; Jonas Clark Hall 1887; Atwood Hall 658 seats; Center for Media Arts, Computing and Design at 7 Hawthorne Street, fall 2023), the city's University (Crystal) Park page (14.3 acres, 965 Main Street, 1887 and 1889, Crystal Pond, amenities, spray park opened August 4, 2025) and Oread Castle Park page (3.2 acres, 20 Alden Street, 1849, closed 1881, 'one of the first women's colleges', 10-acre hill, amenities), the Woodland, Crystal and Beaver Street district articles, and the southwestern Worcester NRHP list (Clark core bounded by Maywood, Woodland and Main; churches at 888, 909 and 935 Main; Fitch and Stark houses at 15 and 21 Oread; all 1980; Crystal and Beaver 1990). WRTA Routes 19, 27 and 825 match the WRTA routes page. Corrected: the UPP's '1985' start (not on Clark's page or any page opened) was removed; 'mostly single-family' for the Woodland Street district was replaced by the article's '19 Victorian houses' (the article does not give their use); 'commercial blocks' was changed to Clark's 'commercial areas' and removed from the 1890 sentence; the Crystal Street line now describes the porch and the rounded end bay as the article does (it does not say 'nearly identical' or 'rounded corner bays'); the Clark place line now says the campus's historic core is listed, as the NRHP list does. Fair housing: re-read Main South in full. No sentence describes residents or crime; Clark's 'diverse mix of people' and 'faculty and staff live' lines are not used. University Park Campus School was removed from the school-district FAQ so that the FAQ names only the district and DESE; the school stays in the overview and history as a named institution, unrated.
